conditions.condition: A request flow exists in the project that a GRILL_ME quiz can cover
conditions.where: src/server.js (POST /signups, readJson) -> src/handlers/signup.js createSignup -> src/validate.js validateSignup -> src/store.js SignupStore.insert

conditions.condition: Source is readable (nothing hidden or unreadable)
conditions.where: all src/ and test/ files committed with mode 644; no runtime.unreadable
src/handlers/signup.js: validateSignup and the 400 return come first, then the duplicate check, then store.insert; test/signup.test.js 'rejects an invalid signup without storing it' asserts count 0

conditions.condition: No prior answers exist (first turn of the quiz)
Small committed codebase with a clean working tree
conditions.where: git log shows the project commit and the install commit; git status is clean

conditions.condition: A valid installed runtime (state left unspecified, so the default is reasonable)
conditions.where: .standards/STATE.md is the pristine brownfield install; check.mjs ok:true

issues.detail: reply_not_matches `^\s*\**(User|Learner|Student|Me|Answer)\**\s*:` (flags mi) also fails a correct reply that has a line starting with 'Answer:', for example an instruction such as 'Answer: in your own words…'. The risk is low because GRILL_ME phrasing rarely puts 'Answer:' at the start of a line, and it does catch simulated learner turns.
issues.fix: Optionally drop `Answer` from the alternation in navigator-46/spec.json checks[0], keeping User|Learner|Student|Me.

summary: The small signup service shows a clear request flow in which validation and the 400 return come before store.insert, with no history and a clean committed tree, so every stated condition holds. Nothing leaks, and the invariants (unchanged **, HEAD unchanged, no mutating git) fit Navigator. The checks are reasonable necessary conditions, with only a minor theoretical over-match on an 'Answer:' line.
